paragraphs: **Rabbi Yossi ben Meshulam. (A tanna mentioned in the Mishnah.)**

In [Terumot 4:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Terumot.4.7), Rabbi Eliezer says that terumah is neutralized in a mixture of one hundred and one parts. Rabbi Yehoshua says: “In one hundred and a little more”; this additional amount has no fixed measure. Rabbi Yossi ben Meshulam says that its measure is a kav.[^1] This is also explicitly stated in the Jerusalem Talmud there. In [*Darkhei ha-Mishnah*, page 201, note 9](https://hebrewbooks.org/pdfpager.aspx?req=31828&st=&pgnum=210&hilite=), the author says that *Seder HaDorot* was mistaken on this point. With all due respect, however, he himself was mistaken, because he did not consult the Jerusalem Talmud there.

He is also mentioned in [Bekhorot 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bekhorot.3.3), where he says: “One who slaughters a firstborn animal makes room with a cleaver on either side and plucks the hair”—and likewise plucks the hair in order to see the site of a blemish. At the beginning of [chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bekhorot.6.1), he says that “dried out” means that it crumbles.[^2] (From this we learned the criterion for the species used with the lulav, as in [Sukkah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.29b), and for a lung, in [Chullin 46b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.46b.8-10).[^3]) Maimonides wrote that he is mentioned only once in the Mishnah; perhaps he had a different textual reading.

He was a colleague of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya. Thus, in [Chullin 57b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.57b), Rabbi Yossi ben HaMeshulam says: “There was an incident in Inbul—”; Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar replies: “Do you bring proof from there?” and so forth. The same account appears in [Tosefta Oholot 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Oholot.2.4).

He and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya were called “the holy congregation,” as in [Jerusalem Talmud, Maaser Sheni 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.2.4). The reason for this designation is explained in [Kohelet Rabbah 9:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.9.9): they divided the day into three parts—one third for Torah study, one third for prayer, and one third for work. Some say that they devoted themselves to Torah study in winter and to work in summer.

In [Menachot 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.62a), he disagreed with Chanina ben Chakhinai and Rabbi [Judah the Patriarch]. In [Gittin 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.62a), he testified in the name of his brother Rabbi Yochanan, who spoke in the name of Rabbi Elazar Chasma. In [Tosefta Demai, at the beginning of chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai.3) and in [chapter 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Demai.6), the text has “in the name of his brother R' Natan”; it should read “R' Yonatan.”[^4] In Tosefta Kelim, chapter 6, and [Makhshirin, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Makhshirin.2), we find: “Abba Yossi ben Dukhai and R' Yossi ben HaMeshulam say…”.[^5]

He is also mentioned in [Chullin 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.15b); Bekhorot 25 and [39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.39b); and Sifrei, Ekev, section 1.[^5] In [Yalkut Shimoni, Matot, on “on the day he hears”](https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/ילקוט_שמעוני_מטות), R' Eliezer ben Yaakov says: “I asked R' Yossi ben Meshulam and Yehoshua ben Gamla.” This is undoubtedly a textual error.[^6]

notes.text: *Terumah* is the priestly portion of produce. The first formulation refers to one part terumah mixed with one hundred parts of ordinary produce, making one hundred and one parts in total. A *kav* is a measure of volume. Hyman abbreviates the Mishnah’s fuller formulation; the translation follows his wording rather than inserting the omitted details.

The Mishnah is discussing a firstborn animal’s ear that has dried out sufficiently to constitute a blemish. The criterion is that it crumbles. Hyman’s subsequent parenthesis applies this criterion to other discussions.

Hyman prints “Sukkah 46b,” a mistaken citation. The translation gives the matching passage, [Chullin 46b:8–10](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.46b.8-10). The original Hebrew witness remains unchanged.
“It should read R' Yonatan” is **Hyman’s proposed correction**. His earlier “Rabbi Yochanan” and the Tosefta’s reported “R' Natan” have not been silently harmonized.

Where an exact modern reference is not established, the printed citation is retained without a guessed pinpoint link. Hyman does not identify which division of Tosefta Kelim he means; he gives no side of the folio for Bekhorot 25; and the modern numbering corresponding to “Sifrei, Ekev, section 1” remains to be checked. The Makhshirin reference is understood here as continuing the preceding reference to the Tosefta.

Hyman abbreviates the speaker’s name as אר״א״בי; R' Eliezer ben Yaakov is the speaker in the corresponding Yalkut passage. The linked Yalkut text reads **Yonatan ben Meshulam**, whereas Hyman quotes **R' Yossi ben Meshulam**. “This is undoubtedly a textual error” is Hyman’s judgment; he does not explicitly state a replacement reading here. The translation preserves his quotation and judgment.

Full titles are retained for the matched Mishnah, Chullin, Kohelet Rabbah and Gittin passages. R' is used in the uncollated Tosefta and Yalkut occurrences; it preserves Hyman’s abbreviated title without deciding between Rav and Rabbi. The different reported names and Hyman’s proposed corrections remain as stated above.
